title: Fitted furniture for rental properties — what landlords get wrong
description: Most landlords treat fitted furniture as a cost to minimise. The smart ones treat it as an investment that reduces voids and increases rental value.
author: Sturij

standfirst.text: Most landlords treat fitted furniture as a cost to minimise. The smart ones treat it as an investment that reduces voids and increases rental value.

body.text: The default landlord approach to fitted furniture is to spend as little as possible. Flatpack wardrobes from a big-box store, assembled on site, with budget hinges and laminate finishes. The logic is understandable: tenants will damage it, so why invest? Replace it cheaply when it falls apart.
body.heading: The false economy

body.text: This logic fails on its own terms. Budget furniture in a rental property typically lasts 3-5 years before doors sag, drawers stick, and surfaces chip. Replacement means another purchase, another assembly, and a period where the property is less presentable. Over a 15-year period, a landlord might replace budget wardrobes three or four times.

Quality fitted furniture changes the equation in ways most landlords don't consider. Well-built wardrobes with Blum hinges and proper edging don't just last longer — they make the property more attractive to better tenants. In a competitive rental market, built-in storage is consistently cited as a deciding factor, particularly for professional tenants who expect a finished home, not a furnished shell.
body.heading: What tenants actually value

body.text: What tenants value is function and feel. Doors that close properly. Drawers that glide. Enough hanging space and shelving to actually live with. Internal lighting is a surprisingly effective differentiator in rental viewings — it reads as quality immediately. None of this requires premium materials. It requires competent specification of mid-range materials with good hardware.

For rental specification, we typically recommend Egger's ST9 texture in neutral tones — whites, light greys, or pale woodgrains. These are the most forgiving finishes for wear and cleaning. Hardware should be Blum or equivalent — CLIP top hinges with BLUMOTION, TANDEMBOX drawers. These components are designed for commercial cycle counts and will outlast the tenancy.
body.heading: Specification for durability

body.text: Handles should be robust and timeless. Simple stainless steel bar handles or routed grip profiles (no handle at all — a channel cut into the door edge) avoid the dated look that decorative handles acquire within a few years. The furniture should feel current in a decade without any updates.

Run the numbers over ten years. Three sets of budget wardrobes at £800 each, plus assembly costs, plus the void days during replacement: roughly £3,000-3,500. One set of fitted wardrobes at £2,500-3,000, installed once, lasting the full period with no maintenance beyond occasional hinge adjustment: the fitted option costs less over the period and delivers higher rental income throughout.
body.heading: The numbers

body.text: The investment case is strongest for HMO and professional rental properties where tenant expectations are highest and void costs are most painful. But even for a single buy-to-let, the maths consistently favours building it properly once over replacing it repeatedly.
